title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

reading.body:
This is a case of infrastructure running before it was authorised to run. The generators at the Vineland site were installed and operated without the permits New Jersey requires under its Air Pollution Control Act, which means the failure sits at the commissioning stage of a deployment, the point where equipment is switched on and the paperwork that is supposed to precede that step is either missing or never obtained. The state did not learn about it from the operator. Inspectors found the 62 generators themselves in late July.

Catching this would not have required a technical control. It would have required a permit check before the generators were energised, and an internal compliance step that treated the permit as a precondition for operation rather than a formality to be settled later. The fine, described by officials as the largest ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey, was the consequence of that check happening outside the company instead of inside it.

The reporting does not establish that the omission was deliberate, and a fine is a regulatory finding rather than proof of intent. The federal lawsuit brought by homeowners over noise is an allegation that has not been adjudicated, and the county health department's violation orders are separate from the state air pollution action. Nothing in the reports establishes which workloads the campus supports or whether any of the generators were running in service of a specific computing task.

reports.title: Data Center Is Fined $1.1 Million for Operating 62 Power Generators

summary:
New Jersey fined DataOne $1.07 million after state inspectors found 62 natural-gas generators at its Vineland data center construction site in late July. The 2,000-kilowatt generators did not have required permits to be installed or operated. Officials said this was the largest fine ever issued to a data center operator in New Jersey for violating the Air Pollution Control Act.

The Vineland campus is planned as a 2.6 million-square-foot complex that will need 350 megawatts of power, enough for a medium-size city, and is slated for completion at the end of the year. Some of the complex is already in use. Homeowners have filed a federal lawsuit against DataOne over persistent noise, and the Cumberland County Health Department has issued violation orders for excessive noise.
